segments.text: > Part of the [Implementation Status](README.md) index. Node's classic `EventEmitter` base class (`require('events')`) — not the same thing as the WHATWG `EventTarget`/`Event`/`CustomEvent` trio tracked in [EVENTS-CANCELLATION.md](EVENTS-CANCELLATION.md). Real Node code uses `EventEmitter` pervasively: `stream.Readable`/`Writable` (see [STREAMS.md](STREAMS.md)'s Node section), `child_process`'s spawned handles, and `net.Server`/sockets all extend it.

rows.feature: `new EventEmitter<T>()` / extending it via `class X extends EventEmitter<T>`
caveats: An override's declared signature isn't checked for compatibility against the method it replaces (tsc's TS2416) — a wildly-wrong override signature is the author's problem ([ADR-00631](../adr/ADR-00631.md))

The checker types every event as taking `...args: any[]`: @types/node types a typed map's listeners through conditional types (`Key`/`Args`/`Listener`), which it does not model yet. A typed map's event names and argument types are checked by code generation instead, not reported as TypeScript errors
`EventEmitter`'s constructor options (`captureRejections`) are a clean rejection
notes: Import it from `events` (named, default or namespace): it is not a global. With no type argument every event takes any arguments (@types/node's default event map); a type argument is an event map of argument tuples (`EventEmitter<{ data: [chunk: string]; end: [] }>`). A subclass constructor calls `super()`

A class in an EventEmitter-rooted tree may **override** any EventEmitter method (`on`/`once`/`emit`/`off`/`removeListener`/`removeAllListeners`/`listenerCount`/`eventNames`) by declaring it — the override wins at every call site (statically and virtually through the vtable), and `super.<method>(...)` reaches the underlying behavior (the nearest ancestor override, else the built-in dispatch), including multi-level `B extends A extends EventEmitter` chains ([TDD-00157](../tdd/TDD-00157.md)/[ADR-00631](../adr/ADR-00631.md))
`x instanceof EventEmitter` answers as a compile-time constant, true for emitters and classes extending one ([ADR-00303](../adr/ADR-00303.md)). See LANGUAGE-CONSTRUCTS.md's `class`/`extends` note
Single inheritance, not composition: a class can extend `EventEmitter` *or* another base, never both — real JS/TS has the same single-inheritance constraint, so this isn't specific to this compiler

caveats: A map-typed emitter requires a string-literal event name at every call site
A `function` listener can't read `this` (the emitter, in Node): a compile error
A listener parameter holding an array with a default value is a clean rejection
notes: Every listener is held as a dynamic function, so emitters of any event map share one representation; a listener's parameters are typed from its event's tuple (or `any` on an untyped emitter), and it may take fewer parameters than the event passes ([ADR-00392](../adr/ADR-00392.md))

caveats: A map-typed emitter requires a string-literal event name
notes: Synchronously invokes every registered listener for `event`, in registration order; returns whether any listener ran; a `once` listener is removed before it runs
`emit(event, a, b, …)` passes each argument; a typed map's event takes exactly its tuple's arguments ([ADR-00392](../adr/ADR-00392.md))

`off`/`removeListener` removes the most recently added matching listener and keeps the others in order; `removeAllListeners()` (no arg) clears every event; `removeAllListeners(event)` clears just that one

caveats: A map-typed emitter requires a string-literal event name
notes: `prepend*` puts the listener before the existing ones ([ADR-01162](../adr/ADR-01162.md))
`eventNames()` returns registration order; an event whose last listener is removed leaves the list, as in Node
caveats: Event names are strings; a symbol event name is not supported

notes: An unlistened `'error'` throws its argument when it is an Error, and otherwise an Error reading `Unhandled error. (<value>)`, as Node does. Resolved at the `.emit()` call site — no runtime cost when the event name isn't `'error'` beyond the `strcmp` itself
caveats: A non-Error, non-string argument is rendered with `String()` in the `Unhandled error. (…)` message, where Node uses `util.inspect`

On a typed map, a mixed-type multi-argument event is a clean rejection (homogeneous arrays only) and a payload-less one is deferred ([ADR-00675](../adr/ADR-00675.md)); on an untyped emitter the result is the `any[]` arguments
notes: Returns a Promise that resolves with the event's argument array the first time it fires; `const arr = await once(ee, 'x')`

caveats: Same payload rules as `once`: on a typed map, mixed-type multi-argument, payload-less, and non-scalar payloads are clean rejections; on an untyped emitter each item is the `any[]` arguments
The buffer is unbounded (Node's default); iterator `.return()`/`.throw()` unregistering the listener is a deferred follow-up ([ADR-00677](../adr/ADR-00677.md))
notes: An async iterator yielding the event's argument array on each emission (`for await (const [x] of on(ee, 'data'))`), buffering events between iterations and parking the consumer when the queue drains; the listener attaches eagerly at the `on(...)` call. Built on the array-yielding generators of [ADR-00676](../adr/ADR-00676.md)
